content.value_statement: Async errors, shared mutations, and weak validation can make JavaScript behavior unreliable. This skill guides focused fixes using modern language features and defensive runtime practices.
actual_capabilities: Guide fixes for equality, coercion, optional chaining, and nullish defaulting errors.
Recommend promise error handling, concurrent operations, and cancellation with AbortController.
Review input validation, HTML sanitization, and safer handling of untrusted text.
Suggest immutable data transformations, copying array methods, and safe numeric representations.
Identify cleanup needs for listeners, timers, observers, and object references.
Guide TypeScript strict typing, unknown narrowing, and exhaustive union handling.
limitations: Provides written guidance, not a bundled executable, test suite, or automated analyzer.
React rendering and UI design are outside the stated scope.
Modern API recommendations require compatibility checks for the target runtime.
Does not include performance measurements or guarantee that suggested changes improve speed.

use_cases.title: Correct asynchronous workflows
use_cases.description: Review promise handling, asynchronous loops, cancellation, and independent operations in application logic.

use_cases.title: Review browser safety and cleanup
use_cases.description: Check untrusted DOM content, listener teardown, timers, and retained object references during frontend reviews.

use_cases.title: Strengthen TypeScript boundaries
use_cases.description: Improve external data checks, unknown narrowing, union models, and exported function types.

prompt_templates.title: Explain unexpected defaults
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this JavaScript expression: [expression]. Explain why zero or an empty string receives the fallback, and suggest a nullish default.

prompt_templates.title: Fix asynchronous iteration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this async loop: [code]. Explain completion and rejection behavior, then suggest sequential or concurrent processing based on [requirements].

prompt_templates.title: Review a data boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript data boundary: [code]. Identify missing runtime validation, unsafe assertions, and HTML risks. Suggest strict types and defensive checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit lifecycle and concurrency
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this module: [code]. Evaluate stale requests, cancellation, retained references, event cleanup, and exhaustive states. Prioritize fixes and identify runtime compatibility constraints.

output_examples.input: My async forEach finishes before all updates complete.
output: forEach does not await promises returned by its callback.
Use sequential iteration when updates depend on earlier results.
For independent updates, collect promises and await their combined completion.
Handle rejections explicitly so failed updates remain visible.

output_examples.input: A zero quantity becomes the default quantity.
output: Logical OR treats zero as a missing value because zero is falsy.
Use nullish coalescing when only null and undefined should trigger the default.
Check zero, empty strings, null, and undefined against the intended behavior.

output_examples.input: A browser module leaks memory after repeated mounting and teardown.
output: Review listeners, observers, and timers that remain active after teardown.
Check closures for references to detached DOM nodes.
Use WeakMap for object metadata when the metadata must not retain its keys.
WeakRef collection timing is nondeterministic and cannot replace explicit cleanup.

best_practices: Provide the relevant code, expected behavior, error details, and target runtime.
Validate external data at boundaries and keep untrusted text away from executable and HTML sinks.
Verify changes with focused tests, linting, and runtime compatibility checks.
anti_patterns: Use async callbacks in forEach when completion must be awaited.
Trust TypeScript assertions or TrustedHTML types without runtime validation or sanitization.
Leave stale requests, listeners, observers, and timers active after teardown.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this skill cover TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends strict typing, unknown narrowing, unions, exhaustive switches, and explicit return types for exported functions.

faq.question: Does it cover React rendering or UI design?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly places React rendering and UI design in separate workflows.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies or run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No bundled installer or test runner is included. It recommends linting, formatting, CI checks, and careful dependency selection.

faq.question: Does the fetch example send information to a service?
faq.answer: It demonstrates cancellation using a placeholder URL. It names no service and includes no sensitive payload or instruction to execute the request.

faq.question: Are all recommended APIs available in older runtimes?
faq.answer: No. Check support for copying array methods, structuredClone, AbortController, and other modern APIs before adopting them.
